prompt: Two teachers compare final exam scores. A random sample from Class A has mean $\bar{x}_A = 82.4$; a random sample from Class B has mean $\bar{x}_B = 78.9$. What is the point estimate for $\mu_A - \mu_B$?
hint: The natural estimate of a difference in population means is the difference in sample means.

hints.text: The natural estimate of a difference in population means is the difference in sample means.
Compute $\bar{x}_A - \bar{x}_B$, keeping the order A minus B.

explanation: The parameter is $\mu_A - \mu_B$; its point estimate is $\bar{x}_A - \bar{x}_B$.
Class A scored 3.5 points higher on average in these samples. Whether that gap is statistically significant depends on the spreads and sample sizes.

alternativeExplanations.title: Order matters
steps: If you had defined the parameter as $\mu_B - \mu_A$, the estimate would be $-3.5$.
Always subtract in the same order as the parameter you wrote down.
Here it is A minus B: $+3.5$.
